exampleFr: Ma meuf travaille dans le même quartier que moi.
exampleEn: My girlfriend works in the same neighborhood as me.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'femme' (woman): fem-me → meuf, by inverting and clipping the syllables.

exampleFr: Les keufs ont contrôlé sa voiture hier soir.
exampleEn: The cops checked his car last night.
collocations: se faire arrêter par les keufs
mnemonic: Verlan of 'flic' (cop), itself already slang for 'policier': flic → keuf.

exampleFr: On organise une teuf chez Sami samedi soir.
exampleEn: We're throwing a party at Sami's place Saturday night.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'fête' (party): fê-te → teuf, by inverting the syllables.

exampleFr: Mon reuf vient me chercher à la gare.
exampleEn: My brother is picking me up at the station.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'frère' (brother): frè-re → reuf, by inverting and clipping.

exampleFr: Ma reus m'a prêté sa veste pour ce soir.
exampleEn: My sister lent me her jacket for tonight.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'sœur' (sister): sœur → reus, by inverting the sounds.

exampleFr: C'est qui, ce keum là-bas ?
exampleEn: Who's that guy over there?
mnemonic: Verlan of 'mec' (guy): mec → keum, by inverting the consonant-vowel order.

exampleFr: Ce type a un comportement zarbi depuis ce matin.
exampleEn: That guy has been acting weird since this morning.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'bizarre': bi-zarre → zar-bi, by swapping the two syllables.

exampleFr: Il est trop vénère parce qu'on a raté le bus.
exampleEn: He's really pissed off because we missed the bus.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'énervé' (annoyed/angry), reshaped by inverting and stressing the syllables.

exampleFr: Le mec au fond du bar avait l'air chelou.
exampleEn: The guy at the back of the bar looked shady.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'louche' (shady/suspicious): lou-che → che-lou, by swapping the syllables.

exampleFr: C'était un concert ouf, on a adoré.
exampleEn: It was a crazy concert, we loved it.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'fou' (crazy): fou → ouf, simply by reversing the two letters.

exampleFr: Arrête, tu es trop relou avec tes questions !
exampleEn: Stop it, you're so annoying with your questions!
mnemonic: Verlan of 'lourd' (heavy, here meaning tiresome): lourd → relou, by inverting the sounds.

exampleFr: Cimer pour le coup de main, frérot.
exampleEn: Thanks for the help, bro.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'merci' (thanks): mer-ci → ci-mer, by swapping the two syllables.

exampleFr: Il parle super bien céfran pour quelqu'un qui vient d'arriver.
exampleEn: He speaks French really well for someone who just arrived.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'français': fran-çais → cé-fran, by inverting and reshaping the syllables.

exampleFr: Je prends le tromé tous les matins pour aller bosser.
exampleEn: I take the subway every morning to go to work.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'métro' (subway): mé-tro → tro-mé, by inverting the two syllables.

en: a person born in France to North African immigrant parents
exampleFr: Le film raconte l'histoire d'un jeune beur dans les années 1980.
exampleEn: The film tells the story of a young 'beur' in the 1980s.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'arabe': a-ra-be → beur (via the intermediate form 'arbe'), coined in the early 1980s and later reclaimed in French media (e.g. 'la Marche des Beurs').

exampleFr: Deux policiers ripoux ont été arrêtés pour corruption.
exampleEn: Two corrupt cops were arrested for bribery.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'pourri' (rotten, here meaning corrupt): pour-ri → ri-pou, popularized by the 1984 film 'Les Ripoux'.

exampleFr: Dans les années 80, on disait 'chébran' pour dire 'branché'.
exampleEn: In the 1980s, people said 'chébran' to mean 'trendy'.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'branché' (trendy/plugged-in): bran-ché → ché-bran, a classic (now slightly dated) 1980s verlan word.

en: to catch, to grab; to hook up with
exampleFr: Il a pécho son numéro à la fin de la soirée.
exampleEn: He got her number by the end of the party.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'choper' (to catch/grab, itself already slang): cho-per → pé-cho, by inverting the syllables.

exampleFr: Zyva, dépêche-toi, on va être en retard !
exampleEn: Come on, hurry up, we're going to be late!
mnemonic: A verlan-style twist on 'vas-y' (go on/come on), reshaping the sounds into 'zyva'.

exampleFr: Laisse béton, ça ne sert à rien de discuter avec lui.
exampleEn: Forget it, there's no point arguing with him.
mnemonic: From Renaud's 1978 song: 'béton' is verlan of 'tomber', so 'laisse béton' is a playful twist on 'laisse tomber' (drop it/forget it).

en: flat out, all the way, at full speed
exampleFr: Il roulait à donf sur l'autoroute.
exampleEn: He was driving flat out on the highway.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'à fond' (all the way/full blast): fond → donf, by inverting the sounds.

exampleFr: Il écoute de la zicmu à fond dans sa chambre.
exampleEn: He blasts music in his room.
mnemonic: Verlan of 'musique' (music): mu-sique → zic-mu; often clipped further to just 'zic'.

exampleFr: Le mec à côté de moi n'arrêtait pas de parler.
